facts.state_of_play: Country music legend Dolly Parton has died at age 80, her family announced Aug. 25. Her sister Stella Parton revealed Dolly had a secret cancer battle and considered experimental treatment. Her final year included the deaths of her husband and brother, ongoing health struggles, and an abandoned career comeback. She made her final public appearance Aug. 14, appearing energized, and gave a final interview four days before her death saying she still had many things she wanted to achieve. Her family shared her final message to fans, and tributes have poured in from artists including Taylor Swift and Sheryl Crow, while her music streams have surged to make her the most streamed artist globally.

facts.state_of_play: King Charles's letter confirming Harry and Meghan remain non-working royals has prompted a reaction from the couple, who say they are 'surprised' and suspect its timing may be tied to an upcoming security review; their spokesman claims they were not warned in advance, though palace sources dispute this. Separately, it has emerged that Harry and Meghan withdrew their children Archie and Lilibet from a new private UK school after just two days, after their protective convoy became separated in heavy traffic during the school run on the first day of term. Meanwhile, King Harald V of Norway was laid to rest in Oslo, concluding 13 days of national mourning, with Prince William leading the UK delegation and world leaders including Spain's King Felipe, Princess Anne, and Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy attending; Zelenskyy's plane was reportedly nearly struck by a drone shortly after departing Moldova. William also made a surprise public appearance with Catherine at Everton's stadium to launch a new suicide prevention campaign. Separately, a public feud has escalated between King Charles and Princess Diana's brother, Earl Charles Spencer, after Spencer's memoir 'Swan Song: Diana, My Sister' alleged Charles told him days after Diana's 1997 death that she would 'be forgotten soon enough,' and that Charles sounded 'giddily elated, like a lottery winner' in a phone call after her death; Spencer also claims some Palace staff were 'relieved' at Diana's death and details a dispute over the coffin procession arrangements. As the memoir's Daily Mail serialisation continues, new claims have emerged: that Queen Elizabeth offered to restore Diana's HRH title after her death, and that Diana told Spencer 'my husband is in love with his valet' before disclosing plans to divorce Charles. Buckingham Palace issued a rare public rebuttal, breaking its 'never complain, never explain' tradition, while insider reports describe Prince William as 'furious' and King Charles's anger over the claims as immense. Prince Harry said he was 'aware' of the book's contents. Amid the row, William and Catherine visited Rothesay on the Isle of Bute while King Charles attended an AI summit at Dumfries House, which was overshadowed by the memoir controversy.

facts.state_of_play: An Amazon Prime Air Boeing 767 cargo plane (Flight 7598) arriving from Puerto Rico overran a diagonal runway at Miami International Airport shortly before 2 p.m. EDT Sunday, struck two vehicles — a cleaning-company van and an SUV — and caught fire; NTSB says all five people killed were occupants of the van, while five others were injured (three critically); the two-person crew survived. Victims have been identified as Cuban immigrants who had fled Cuba. New video shows a survivor crawling from the plane and a person found alive in a crushed car near the crash site. NTSB recovered the flight data and cockpit voice recorders; initial flight data shows signs consistent with the pilots attempting a go-around before the crash, and investigators are examining whether the plane touched down too far down the runway to stop safely; the aircraft came to rest about 1,300 feet past the runway end. NTSB is set to interview the surviving pilots. All runways closed; FAA and NTSB continue investigating.

quotes.gist: There is a 'real risk' Russian drones could fall on NATO's eastern flank territory and be called an accident.
Russia's hybrid threat to Europe has 'intensified'; ordered measures to protect critical infrastructure and defence sites.
Intelligence suggests Putin is eager to test NATO's will by striking countries assisting Kyiv with a missile strike.
Drone warfare in Ukraine is moving at 'lightning speed'; most NATO countries could not repulse a Russian missile attack if the conflict expands.
Defended Don Jr.'s acceptance of a large gift from Kremlev, saying such presents are common, and said his son repaid him.

facts.state_of_play: Trump reports progress on establishing a permanent US military base in Poland, with a location announcement expected soon. Polish PM Tusk warns that Russia may deliberately or accidentally strike NATO allies, and Western intelligence reportedly indicates Putin is planning a missile strike on a NATO country to test the alliance's resolve, after a Russian attack near western Ukraine forced Poland to close its airspace and scramble fighter jets. Latvian President Edgars Rinkevics has separately warned that Europe is not keeping pace with rapidly evolving drone and aerial warfare in Ukraine, saying most NATO states could not repel a Russian missile attack if the war expands. French President Emmanuel Macron says Russian hybrid attacks against Europe are intensifying and has ordered protection of French infrastructure and defence industry sites, while also calling for an emergency G7 meeting to address soaring energy prices amid the Ukraine and Middle East wars. On the ground, Russia has struck Ukraine's border crossings with Poland and Moldova and its drones are threatening Western officials traveling to Kyiv, even as its eastern offensive appears to be stalling. Separately, Ukraine and Russia are reportedly growing frustrated with US envoy Steve Witkoff and the US-mediated peace process, though Trump is said to see no problem with Witkoff's role. Meanwhile, Russia has begun a three-day parliamentary election - the first since its 2022 invasion of Ukraine - with only parties supporting the war allowed on the ballot; United Russia, which won more than two-thirds of seats in 2021, is expected to retain its dominance amid signs of economic strain among voters, and has used celebrities like NHL star Alex Ovechkin in its campaign. Separately, Latvia has imposed an indefinite entry ban on Ovechkin and sanctioned oligarch Umar Kremlev, a close Putin associate who also has financial ties to Donald Trump Jr. Amid Republican criticism over the propriety of Trump Jr. accepting a lavish Bahamas wedding party from Kremlev, Trump Jr. has repaid Kremlev for the party, and President Trump has publicly defended the arrangement, calling such gifts common.
